title: Ten test cases, one noisy score
hook: A model scores 6 out of 10 on fresh cases. Is it a 60% model?

knows: that a model should be tested on held-out data
doesNotKnow: that a small test set gives a noisy score
that the noise shrinks only with more test cases

misconception: A good (or bad) score on a handful of held-out cases proves how good the model is.
objective: The learner can explain that a test score is itself a random measurement, that on 10 cases an 80% model often scores far from 80%, and that more held-out cases are what make the score trustworthy.

claims.text: The toy model is right on each fresh case with probability 0.8, independently; one test draws 10 (or 100, or 1,000) cases and counts how many it gets right.
claims.source: The lesson's own model in Demo.tsx (TRUE_ACC, runTest). Draws use mulberry32 seed 1, untuned, restarted when the test size changes (the learner's 10-case runs are kept and the stream continues after them); the counts on stage depend on how many tests the learner runs.

claims.text: For a model truly right 80% of the time, a test of 10 cases gives 6 or fewer right with probability 12.1%, about 1 in 8.
claims.source: Binomial(10, 0.8): P(X ≤ 6) = 0.1209 (exact sum; computed by binomCdf(10, 0.8, 6) in Demo.tsx and by an independent script by the category manager).

claims.text: The score's typical spread is about 12.6 points either way at 10 cases and about 1.3 points at 1,000 cases.
claims.source: Standard deviation of a proportion: 100 × √(0.8 × 0.2 / n) = 12.65 at n = 10 and 1.26 at n = 1,000 (spreadPts in Demo.tsx).

claims.text: Only more held-out cases shrink the noise in a test score.
claims.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §7.2 (test error estimation needs enough held-out data). Within the toy the spread depends only on n (derivation above); 'only' is about the score of a fixed model. · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: DISPUTED. 'Only' is a universal the source does not support: ESL 2e 7.2 discusses held-out test error but not that sample size is the sole lever; stratified or paired evaluation also cuts score variance for a fixed model. Within the toy (iid cases, fixed p) SD = sqrt(p(1-p)/n) depends on n alone, so the scoped claim is true. Fix (builder): drop 'Only', e.g. 'More held-out cases shrink the noise: the spread falls as 1/sqrt(n)', or scope it to this toy; then re-cite as derivation.

recall.question: Two chatbots are each tried on 10 questions. Bot A gets 9 right, bot B gets 7. What can you conclude?
options: Not much: on 10 questions scores that far apart happen by chance
A is clearly the better bot
recall.why: A score on 10 cases is a noisy measurement: an 80% model lands anywhere from 6 to 10 quite often. To tell two models apart you need many more test cases.
